Definition: of Hebrew origin (H5992); Aminadab, an Israelite:--Aminadab.
BiblicalUsage: Once in each genealogy, a link in the line of the Messiah: Aram begat Aminadab, and Aminadab begat Naasson, and Naasson begat Salmon. Luke counts him the same way, the son of Aram and the father of Naasson, in the line that runs from Abraham to David to Jesus; the name is a link in the chain, and the link is all the Bible says of him.
TheologicalSignificance: A name in the genealogy of Christ carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is the chain itself, that the promise runs father to son through men whose only story is the son they begat.
